extra.message: User-controlled input from request.args.get('search') is interpolated directly into a SQLAlchemy text() clause via an f-string: text(f"text like '%{search_param}%'"). This is passed to .filter() and executed as raw SQL, allowing SQL injection (e.g. boolean/UNION-based extraction of other users' private notes or arbitrary data).

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: The registration code submitted by the user (form.registration_code.data) is concatenated directly into a raw SQL query string passed to session.execute(text(...)) without parameterization: "SELECT id, code FROM ... WHERE code = '{code}'". This allows SQL injection, enabling an attacker to bypass registration-code validation and create accounts, or extract data.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: The 'preferences' cookie value (attacker-controlled) is base64-decoded and passed to pickle.loads() in the before_request handler. Deserializing untrusted pickle data allows arbitrary code execution via a crafted __reduce__ payload, leading to full remote code execution.

urlopen() is called on a URL fully controlled by the user (form.url.data from the /account/image route flows into get_base64_image_blob -> download). No validation of scheme or host is performed, allowing Server-Side Request Forgery (access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints) and also local file reads via the file:// scheme.

The update_account POST handler lacks the @login_required decorator (unlike the GET /account route), so authorization is not enforced at the route level. It mutates current_user and commits, exposing account modification functionality without an authentication guard.

current_user.__dict__.update(filtered_values) blindly applies all submitted form fields (including the 'is_admin' BooleanField defined in AccountForm) to the user object before commit. A normal user can submit is_admin=true to escalate their own privileges to administrator (mass assignment / privilege escalation).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /accounts/<int:user_id>/notes route returns ALL notes for an arbitrary user_id supplied in the URL, with no check that user_id matches current_user.id. The query does not filter on Note.private, so any authenticated user can read any other user's private notes (Insecure Direct Object Reference / broken access control).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: delete_note fetches the note by the user-supplied note_id and deletes it without verifying that note.user_id == current_user.id. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's notes by guessing/iterating note IDs (Insecure Direct Object Reference / broken access control).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The 404 error handler passes an f-string containing request.path (attacker-controlled) into render_template_string(). Jinja2 evaluates the string as a template, so a crafted URL path containing template syntax leads to Server-Side Template Injection and potential remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: Flask app.secret_key is hardcoded to a trivial, predictable value ('super secret key'). The session/cookie signing key being public allows an attacker to forge signed session cookies and bypass authentication or impersonate users.

A static, hardcoded registration code ('a36e990b-0024-4d55-b74a-f8d7528e1764') is seeded into the database. Anyone who knows this value (it is in source control) can register a new account without an admin-issued code, undermining the registration access control.

The 'preferences' cookie is set without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite flags. Combined with it being a base64-pickle blob deserialized server-side, the missing flags also make it client-readable/modifiable; the cookie is exposed to JavaScript and transmittable over plaintext HTTP.

The SQLAlchemy engine is created with echo=True, causing all SQL statements (including those containing sensitive data and credentials being inserted/queried) to be logged. This can leak sensitive information into application logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
